recipes.name: Indian Chicken Curry I
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon finely chopped fresh ginger root

steps.text: Rinse chicken and pat dry; season with salt and pepper to taste. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium high heat, then saute chicken until browned. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Saute onions in skillet until translucent; add ginger and garlic and saute until fragrant, then stir in curry powder.
Return chicken to skillet and add tomato sauce, coconut milk, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon stick. Season with salt to taste and stir all together.
Reduce heat to low and simmer until chicken is tender and cooked through (no longer pink inside), about 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Indian Chicken Curry I
raw_recipe.description: My friend's father, who is from India, showed me how to make this. It's delicious! Serve with hot cooked rice.

review.reviewBody:
This is a really easy, great-tasting recipe that my husband loves and I've received compliments on. Here are some modifications I make:
1) I double the curry powder. (I use regular supermarket curry powder.) I do like the taste of curry to really come out, and I tend to like things spicy (though not so spicy that you can't taste the actual food).
2) I use diced tomatoes instead of tomato sauce (since I remember one reader saying that the tomato sauce overwhelms the taste of curry.
3) Can't be bothered w/ whole cloves, cinnamon stick, etc.--I just use a pinch or two of cloves, cardamom and cinnamon.
4) If you are on a diet, substituting plain nonfat yogurt for the coconut milk works great--just don't overheat so the yogurt doesn't curdle.

I made this for a group of 15 and followed the recipe with a couple of tweaks. 
I started the sauce 2 days before the dinner then refrigerated it...I did add extra curry (quantity unknown-dash here/there), also 5 large carrots and 5 large potatoes cut into chunks. 
I browned the chicken and added to the simmering sauce about an 30 minutes prior to serving.

We liked it! My Indian landlady from days of yore showed me that you take chicken pieces (legs, thighs, wings, breast, etc., and whack them into smaller bite size servings) leaving the bones in, and fry them in hot oil until they nicely dark brown. Then you toss in the spices and add a blended puree of the cooking liquid blended with your onion and ginger and cook it up until the chicken is tender, adding ample salt. I concur -- using diced tomatoes is much more appropriate than tomato sauce or puree' and adds a lighter tomato flavor which is better. Cook the chicken in the tomato dices and liquid, until it's tender, then at the last 5 minutes add the coconut milk for best flavor. Trust me, this is worth whole spices, just tell the kids to fish them out. Serve with naan, or tortillas, or other flat bread, and a dish of rice -- add a steaming bowl of broccoli and you have your meal done! Remember diced tomatoes in juice, not tomato sauce, cook until the chicken is done and well coated with the spice mixture and wait to add the coconut milk until the last few minutes for best flavor.

Excellent recipe, tried it several times and it became one of family favorites. However, I recommend using boneless, skinless chicken tights since the meat is moister than chicken breasts. I also grill them or broil just a little, they are more flavorful this way.

I changed a few things--cut up a whole chicken; skinned it; after browning chicken, i cooked onions, garlic, and ginger as directed but also added the cinnamon, cloves, and cardamon and toasted that as well. Then, i added the tomato sauce (only 8 oz.) and the coconut milk and stirred. Lastly, i reintroduced the chicken. It's better if u mix the sauce before adding the chicken again. I also added some cayenne peppers (chopped) to the onion mix. The flavor still required tweaking, so i added a tablespoon of ketchup. That seemed to help a lot. I simmered the chicken an hour with a lid on til it fell off the bone and then reduced the sauce til it was a bit thicker. Serve with rice and pappadum!

This turned out to be a nice Indian Curry dish...although I had to tweak it a bit. I disagree that the tomato sauce was a distraction. that would come from someone limited in the different variety of curry dishes-even within only the Indian types.
After feeling this dish needed something more, I added about a 1/2 cup of yogurt, increased the curry by another 1/2 Tablespoon, added 1 Tablespoon brown sugar, doubled the spices and let it simmer about 45 minutes. The second time, not having plain yogurt, I actually tried adding vanilla yogurt, and we actually loved the flavor it added, so I will likely do that next time. Although healthiest with chicken breast, more flavorful with entire chicken or thighs. Nice base recipe to begin with!

This was a good recipe however I changed a few things to suit my family's tastes. I used legs simply because we prefer dark meat. 1 onion instead of 2, added 2 peeled, chopped carrots, 2 medium potatoes cut in large pieces (I pre-boiled these about 7 minutes before adding to be sure they were cooked through) added 1/2 cup green chili. I only used curry powder because I did not have all of the whole herbs, so I doubled the amount of that. Served with basmati rice and peas. My mother-in-law is very picky and she went back for seconds and thirds!

I made this 2 days ago, very tasty. I made some Jasmine rice to go with this, I actually used 8 chicken thighs (skins removed) and boiled them for 30 minutes in an olive oil and smoked salt brine, then pan seared them, I did use twice the amount of curry powder and reduced the tomatoes, but I liked the creaminess that the Coconut brought to the rue. I also added some Anise and fresh cilantro, really made the dish stand out, as far as a "true" curry dish, that could be a matter of taste and opinion, Indian dishes traditionally are very complex in the uses of spices.

All in all, still a good crowd pleaser for comfort food!

Delicious. I used half the tomato sauce as suggested by other reviewers, one tablespoon of hot Indian curry (Guram Masala) as the recipe suggested and another tablespoon of mild curry powder (Garam Masala) to intensify the flavour. Plenty spicy. I also used 8 boneless chicken thighs chopped up instead of bones-in breast, because I prefer dark meat. Yum!
I also used ground spices for the whole spices, doubled the curry powder and added a can of rinsed and drained chickpeas. The whole family loved it. I will be making this again.

I doubled the curry powder, and used the least amount of tomato sauce possible. I added some red and orange bell peppers. Pretty good recipe, just keep in mind the tomato sauce me, it might be better to put a little bit at a time and adjust according to your taste.

This recipe is SO GOOD! I'm not a fan of curry, but this is amazing. For my personal pot, I add fire roasted tomatoes, a half pint of heavy cream, jalapenos, cilantro, saffron, and Serrano peppers. It really brings out the flavor, and gives it just enough kick to clear the sinuses. It's DEFINITELY worth the addition, as it brings out all the other flavors.

I followed the recipe exact (prior to reading the reviews). I immediately noticed the overpowering tomato flavor. I added more curry and still the tomato dominated my palette. I used a lot of curry almost the whole bottle to get the curry flavor to shine through. Not please with the results. This was not a true curry and I won’t be using this recipe again.
I've made this recipe for years and I absolutely love it. It's easy and fairly quick to make and is so delicious. I don't change a thing to the original recipe.
My family loved the flavor. Just wish there was an easier way to strain out the cloves.
not to my taste. I ate it but wouldnt make it again. it was very bland and there was no spice level to it
It tasted like tomato soup to me. I was able to eat it as long as I didn't think of it as curry.

Blended flavors were delightful. I used bone-in thighs, powdered spices, and cut the meat off the bones before putting all back in for the simmer. It takes longer than given. Thank you for this recipe
This was the worst new recipe I’ve ever made. Will never make again!

I've never made curry before, so this was a great introductory recipe. I added a little extra hot curry powder, garlic, and tossed in some red pepper flakes because it wasn't quite hot enough for me, but that was just right. Very good flavors and super easy!
